C2: Condition (ii) of NS-1 is met only marginally: at the moment the driver tapped "I'm Here" (17:19:15) the GPS put him 41 m from the pickup point (F6), i.e. within the 200 m data-layer radius, so the tap itself is not the defect the rider relies on. [F6] [NS-1]

[F3 F9 F10 F12] [NS-1]
C5: Because at least one of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) is not satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider under NS-2 (the rider's own account is a further support: 0 no-show disputes upheld in 90 days, F16). [F4 F7 F16] [NS-2]

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled this RydeX trip as a rider no-show and Ryde recorded a $6.61 cancellation fee against the rider, so the fee's validity is governed by the no-show branch of the policy (NS-0, driver cancelled and alleges no-show).

Condition (iii) of NS-1 fails: the driver stayed within 200 m for only 3 min 40 s after the tap (F6), and no record shows continuous presence at the pickup point beyond 3:01 — the platform-recorded arrival was 17:17:50 and the cancellation 5 min 5 s later (F5), but that arrival timestamp is not the tap and the pre-tap waiting period does not count toward NS-1 (iii).

Although the driver's post-trip statement claims he waited over 3 minutes, the only in-app message announcing the no-show is his 17:22 message "3 min up, cancelling the trip" (F10), which measures his wait from his own 17:19 "I'm here" message (F9) — 3 min 55 s of recorded stationary time from 17:18:50 to cancellation (F3) is largely pre-tap presence that NS-1 (iii) expressly excludes.

Because at least one of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) is not satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider under NS-2 (the rider's own account is a further support: 0 no-show disputes upheld in 90 days, F16).
The refund is $6.61, the exact cancellation fee on the fare record (F7), matching the NS-7 cancellation-fee voucher amount; no surge applied (F8).

The driver's 90-day history shows 3 disputes with 2 upheld, both no-show disputes (F17), which supports asking Ryde to review his use of the cancellation/no-show button alongside the refund; this profile fact is only an additional action, not the basis of the main finding.

No safety element requires escalation: the chat contains only two ordinary trip messages with no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation (F9, F10, F11), and no incident or weather factor is present (F13, F14, F15).

weaknesses: The system records actually favour the driver on conditions (i) and (ii): he tapped "I'm Here" at 17:19:15 only 41 m from the pickup (F6), and was inside the 200 m radius cumulatively 5 min 5 s before cancelling (F2), so the rider cannot argue he never arrived or was far away.

On the face of the timeline the driver cancelled 5 min 5 s after the platform recorded arrival (F5) and after 6 min 55 s of total trip time (F4), which the judge may read as satisfying the policy's "more than 3 minutes" waiting requirement; my case depends on reading NS-1 (iii) strictly from the tap (F6: only 3 min 40 s within 200 m after the tap).

The rider's own complaint — "I came out a minute after the driver cancelled" — is not corroborated by any GPS or timeline fact showing the rider was at the pickup point, and the driver's contemporaneous message (F10) is consistent with a genuine no-show, so the judge could find the rider simply was not there in time.

Conceded: the driver did tap "I'm Here" at 17:19:15 at 41 m from the pickup (F6), which satisfies the arrival-confirmation element; the rider's case rests on the waiting-time element, not on (i)/(ii).

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled this RydeX trip as a rider no-show and Ryde recorded a $6.61 cancellation fee against the rider, so the fee's validity is governed by the no-show branch of the policy (NS-0, driver cancelled and alleges no-show).

Condition (ii) of NS-1 is met only marginally: at the moment the driver tapped "I'm Here" (17:19:15) the GPS put him 41 m from the pickup point (F6), i.e. within the 200 m data-layer radius, so the tap itself is not the defect the rider relies on.

Condition (iii) of NS-1 fails: the driver stayed within 200 m for only 3 min 40 s after the tap (F6), and no record shows continuous presence at the pickup point beyond 3:01 — the platform-recorded arrival was 17:17:50 and the cancellation 5 min 5 s later (F5), but that arrival timestamp is not the tap and the pre-tap waiting period does not count toward NS-1 (iii).

Although the driver's post-trip statement claims he waited over 3 minutes, the only in-app message announcing the no-show is his 17:22 message "3 min up, cancelling the trip" (F10), which measures his wait from his own 17:19 "I'm here" message (F9) — 3 min 55 s of recorded stationary time from 17:18:50 to cancellation (F3) is largely pre-tap presence that NS-1 (iii) expressly excludes.

Because at least one of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) is not satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider under NS-2 (the rider's own account is a further support: 0 no-show disputes upheld in 90 days, F16).
The refund is $6.61, the exact cancellation fee on the fare record (F7), matching the NS-7 cancellation-fee voucher amount; no surge applied (F8).

The driver's 90-day history shows 3 disputes with 2 upheld, both no-show disputes (F17), which supports asking Ryde to review his use of the cancellation/no-show button alongside the refund; this profile fact is only an additional action, not the basis of the main finding.

No safety element requires escalation: the chat contains only two ordinary trip messages with no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation (F9, F10, F11), and no incident or weather factor is present (F13, F14, F15).

weaknesses: The system records actually favour the driver on conditions (i) and (ii): he tapped "I'm Here" at 17:19:15 only 41 m from the pickup (F6), and was inside the 200 m radius cumulatively 5 min 5 s before cancelling (F2), so the rider cannot argue he never arrived or was far away.

On the face of the timeline the driver cancelled 5 min 5 s after the platform recorded arrival (F5) and after 6 min 55 s of total trip time (F4), which the judge may read as satisfying the policy's "more than 3 minutes" waiting requirement; my case depends on reading NS-1 (iii) strictly from the tap (F6: only 3 min 40 s within 200 m after the tap).

The rider's own complaint — "I came out a minute after the driver cancelled" — is not corroborated by any GPS or timeline fact showing the rider was at the pickup point, and the driver's contemporaneous message (F10) is consistent with a genuine no-show, so the judge could find the rider simply was not there in time.

claims.assertion: The driver reached the pickup area and remained there: GPS shows he was first within 200 m of the pickup at 17:17:50 and his closest approach was 35 m at 17:18:45, so the 'at the pick-up location' requirement is met.
The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 17:19:15 while 41 m from the pickup point (within the 200 m arrival radius), satisfying NS-1(i) and (ii).

After the 'I'm Here' tap the driver stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s (> 180 s), and the platform-recorded arrival to cancellation gap was 5 min 5 s, so the continuous-wait requirement in NS-1(iii) is met.

The driver was stationary at 54 m from the pickup point from 17:18:50 until the 17:22:55 cancellation, corroborating that he physically waited at the pickup rather than leaving; the GPS record covers the wait in full with no gap, so no G12 referral is needed.

The rider was given notice and time: the driver's chat messages at 17:19 (arrival at the pickup) and 17:22 ("3 min up, cancelling the trip") were both sent before cancelling, and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped.
Because the driver cancelled on rider no-show with all NS-1 elements satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee stands and no refund is due to the rider.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint ("I came out a minute after the driver cancelled") is not rebutted by any GPS or timeline fact showing when the rider actually appeared; the record only shows the wait ended at 17:22:55, so the rider's timing claim is simply unverified rather than disproved.

The rider will point out that the timeline shows a notional 'platform recorded arrival' at 17:17:50 (F5) while the driver's own 'I'm Here' tap was only at 17:19:15 (F6); measured from the earlier platform arrival the strict 3-minute wait (F5: 5 min 5 s) is satisfied, but the gap between platform-recorded arrival and driver tap may invite argument about which arrival anchors NS-1(iii).

The driver's 90-day record — 3 disputes, 2 upheld, both no-show (F17) — is a profile fact the rider may cite against him and could support a repeated-conduct flag under RD-6/NS-2-type account review, even though profile facts cannot decide this case.
The driver's written statement (F12) is a post-hoc account only; the rider may argue the driver never actually made contact with the rider beyond two chat messages (F9, F10).

points.response: Conceded in part: the GPS does show the driver within 200 m from 17:17:50 and as close as 35 m at 17:18:45 (F1, F2), so NS-1(ii) is not the rider's complaint — but being in the area is only the spatial half of the test, and it does not supply the continuous post-tap wait that NS-1(iii) separately requires.

Conceded: the driver did tap "I'm Here" at 17:19:15 at 41 m from the pickup (F6), which satisfies the arrival-confirmation element; the rider's case rests on the waiting-time element, not on (i)/(ii).

This is the disputed point and the driver's own arithmetic defeats it: NS-1(iii) measures continuous waiting at the pickup point after the tap and until cancellation, and F6 records only 3 min 40 s inside 200 m after the 17:19:15 tap with cancellation at 17:22:55 (F4, F6) — the driver's 17:22 message "3 min up" (F10) likewise counts only from his own 17:19 "I'm here" message (F9), so the longer 5 min 5 s figure (F2, F5) is unavailable because it starts from the 17:17:50 platform arrival, and the driver cannot have it both ways: either (i) was satisfied by the tap (F6) and the wait runs from 17:19:15, or (i) was never done at 17:17:50.

The stationary period F3 proves presence, not compliance with NS-1(iii): it runs from 17:18:50, i.e. largely before the 17:19:15 tap (F6), and the policy counts continuous waiting only after the tap; and although there is no GPS gap requiring a G12 referral, F3's 54 m stand-off and the driver's closest approach of 35 m (F1) show he never came to where the rider could see him.

Two chat messages are not the point — the policy's test is elapsed time after the arrival confirmation, not notice: the "3 min up" message (F10) was sent only 3 min 40 s after the driver's own "I'm here" message (F9) and the trip was cancelled at 17:22:55 (F4), leaving no more than the bare 3 minutes and never the > 3 min (≥ 3:01) that NS-1(iii) demands.

Since NS-1(iii) is not made out from the tap at 17:19:15 (F6), NS-2 applies and the $6.61 must be refunded in full (F7); the driver's 90-day record of 3 disputes with 2 upheld, both no-show (F17), further supports account review of his no-show cancellations, though it is not the basis of the finding.

I withdraw the RD-6 citation from my own claim C7: this dispute is not a route-deviation case, so RD-6 does not apply and the account-review request under NS-2 plus the driver's no-show history (F17) is what I ask the judge to note.
Conceded only as to the branch: the fee is indeed tested under NS-1, and it passes — NS-0 routes a driver-cancels-alleging-no-show case into NS-1, which is satisfied on all three limbs (F1, F2, F6).
Agreed: the tap at 17:19:15 was 41 m from the pickup, so NS-1(ii) is squarely met and not merely marginally.

NS-1(iii) is met on the record: the driver stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap (F6), which is > 3:01, so the rider's assertion that 'no record shows continuous presence beyond 3:01' is contradicted by F6 itself; independently, the timeline records arrival at 17:17:50 and cancellation 5 min 5 s later (F5), also over three minutes.

The premise is wrong: NS-1(iii) counts the time within 200 m after the tap, and F6 records exactly 3 min 40 s of that, so it is not excluded pre-tap presence; the rider's reading of the 17:22 chat message (F10) as starting the clock at the 17:19 message (F9) has no basis in NS-1, whose anchor is the 'I'm Here' tap, not a chat message.

NS-2 is not triggered because all of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) hold: tap made (F6), tap within 200 m at 41 m (F6), and 3 min 40 s continuously within 200 m after the tap while stationary 54 m from the pickup until cancellation (F3, F6); the rider cites no GPS or timeline fact showing the rider was ever at the pickup point, so the no-show stands and the fee remains valid.
The amount is not in dispute ($6.61, no surge), but the outcome is: with NS-1 satisfied the fee is not refundable, so NS-7's voucher form is irrelevant here.

The driver's profile shows 1124 trips in 90 days with only 2 upheld no-show disputes (F17), which is evidence of a working record rather than abuse; in any event RD-6 requires the RD-1/NS violation to be established in this case, and it is not, so no flag_account is warranted.
Agreed: nothing in the chat or the traffic/weather record raises SAFE-1 or SAFE-2, so the case stays with the ordinary no-show rules.
